statement: The geometric monodromy on the 27 lines over the complement of the singular-cubic discriminant in the full projective coefficient space is W(E6), of order 51,840, in its 27-letter action.

answer.qualification: This is geometric monodromy of the unrestricted coefficient family; it is not S27 and is not a specialized arithmetic Galois group.

source.location: Introduction, first paragraph, p. 1: Harris’s computation of the monodromy of the 27 lines on a cubic surface

origin.inheritance_basis: Set n=3 and degree 2n−3=3 in the family classification; Hashimoto–Kadets explicitly recall the cubic-surface monodromy W(E6).

scope: Projective lines on smooth cubic surfaces in P3. Generic complex enumeration, real parameter chambers, and probability distributions on real coefficients are distinguished in individual associations.
notes:
This is geometric monodromy of the unrestricted coefficient family, not the group of every arithmetic specialization. The inspected source is Hashimoto–Kadets, which attributes the theorem to Harris. The stored permutations give a verified transitive realization of W(E6) of order 51,840; they are not asserted to have been extracted from the cited paper.

Originality audit: Harris (1979) is the original attribution. The later Hashimoto–Kadets or Zhan text retained in source is a verification/restatement source, not the original claim. For the n=2 singleton case this record includes an elementary deduction.

Related literature. Galois groups of enumerative problems (Joe Harris, 1979). Historical attribution is retained here. The result’s sole article reference identifies the inspected statement or calculation at the recorded locator.
